title: Add a patterns.md bullet requiring every grep-based acceptance-criterion oracle to be proven falsifiable against main before it is pinned in a PRD
description:
Doc-only. No src change, no rebuild needed.

RECURRENCE, not a one-off. The reviewer has now caught a non-falsifiable acceptance-criterion oracle in two consecutive cycles:

- CAM-363: an AC used a grep piped into another grep (`! grep -n 'stderr' <file> | grep -q \"step: 'clean-tree'\"`) where the second grep could essentially never match, so the assertion passed regardless of the code. Captured in the journal only, and dismissed as a backlog issue because there was no code to change.
- CAM-368 (fingerprint 9f6db2fcc75d): AC6c's oracle `grep -q 'plan-preflight-marker.ts' test/supervisor/plan/plan-preflight.test.ts` was satisfied by an import that ALREADY EXISTED on main, so it would have passed with zero new assertions. The substance landed anyway, so it was not a defect in the diff, but the oracle itself could not have failed.

Diagnosis of why the existing discipline did not catch it: the CAM-368 cycle DID verify oracles against main before dispatch, and all six checked (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC7, AC8, AC11a) were genuinely red. AC6c was simply not among the six. The rule as currently held is 'spot-check the oracles', and a sample is exactly what lets a tautological one through. The rule has to be a SWEEP.

Why patterns.md rather than the journal: the journal is cycle narrative read by the orchestrator after the fact. Acceptance criteria are authored by the subagent-planner, which greps scripts/cam/patterns.md by subsystem/keyword when generating a PRD. Putting the rule in patterns.md is what actually gets it consulted at authoring time by the agent that writes the criteria. The journal-only capture demonstrably did not prevent the recurrence.

PROPOSED BULLET (wording to be refined in implementation), appended to the appropriate section of scripts/cam/patterns.md:

'**Acceptance-criterion oracles must be provably falsifiable.** Before pinning any shell/grep-based acceptance criterion in a PRD, run EVERY one of them against unmodified main and confirm each currently FAILS. Sweep them all, do not spot-check: caught twice by review (CAM-363, CAM-368) where the failing oracle was the one not sampled. Common non-falsifiable shapes: asserting on a string that already exists on main (an import, a filename, an existing symbol); a grep piped into a second grep whose pattern can never match the first grep's output format; asserting presence of something the story does not remove. For a criterion that pins ORDER or CONTENT rather than existence, verify falsifiability by actually inverting the implementation locally, observing the red, and restoring.'

ACCEPTANCE: the bullet exists in scripts/cam/patterns.md, is placed in a section a planner would grep when authoring acceptance criteria, and cites both CAM-363 and CAM-368 as the precedents. Gates green (typecheck, bun test, check:all).

spec.scope: Doc-only. No src/ change, no test change, no rebuild. Append ONE new bullet at the END of scripts/cam/patterns.md stating that any assertion pinned as a verification oracle must be proven falsifiable (proven to currently FAIL against unmodified main) before it is pinned, and that the check is an exhaustive SWEEP of every oracle, never a spot-check of a sample. Widen the rule past the issue's original text to cover BOTH surfaces where the class has now appeared: grep/shell acceptance-criterion oracles authored in PRDs by subagent-planner, AND assertions authored inside test files by subagent-implementer. Additionally extend the existing 'Test quality' clause list in the curated invariants block of scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md with a short falsifiability clause pointing at the new patterns.md bullet, mirroring the established dual-surface precedent (short form in CLAUDE.md loads every story, detailed form in patterns.md is grep-on-demand). The CLAUDE.md half is load-bearing, not decoration: CAM-374 was authored by an implementer writing a tmux dispatch test, who would have grepped patterns.md for 'dispatch'/'tmux' and never for 'falsifiable', so a patterns.md-only fix provably would not have caught the third instance. EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: fixing the weak assertion in test/dispatch.test.ts (that is CAM-374, a separate issue and a separate PR); correcting the pre-existing 'Four clauses' / five-clauses off-by-one in the patterns.md line-776 bullet; any edit to any line of patterns.md above the current EOF; any src/ or test/ change of any kind.
acceptanceCriteria: RED-ON-MAIN (swept, main returns 0): `grep -c 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md` returns 1 or greater.

RED-ON-MAIN (swept, main has no match at all): the new bullet is appended strictly BELOW every pre-existing bullet, i.e. `test "$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)" -gt 897` succeeds. patterns.md is 897 lines on main and its final bullet begins at line 897.

PINNING ORACLE, deliberately GREEN-ON-MAIN (this one is a regression guard on invariance, not a claim about new behavior, and is exempt from the red-first duty by that fact): `sed -n '776p' scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q 'Test-quality convention, expanded'` still succeeds after the change, proving no pre-existing line shifted and that the many `patterns.md:NNN` cross-references elsewhere in the file remain valid.

RED-ON-MAIN (swept): the new bullet cites all three precedents on its own single line: `L=$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q 'CAM-363' && sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q 'CAM-368' && sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q 'CAM-374'`.

RED-ON-MAIN (swept): the new bullet covers BOTH authoring surfaces, not just PRDs. Its line matches case-insensitively on an acceptance-criterion term AND on a test-assertion term: `L=$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -qi 'acceptance' && sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -qi 'test assertion'`.

RED-ON-MAIN (swept, main returns 0): the curated invariants block gains a short falsifiability clause: `grep -c 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md` returns 1 or greater, and that clause is inside the existing 'Test quality' bullet rather than added as a new standalone invariant bullet.

HOUSE STYLE, conditional on AC1 having matched (this oracle is vacuously true if AC1 fails, so it is only meaningful when read together with AC1): the new bullet is a single unwrapped line starting with `- **`, carries no `[resolved` prefix, and contains no em-dash character, per the no-em-dash-in-persisted-md rule at patterns.md:24. Verify with `L=$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q '^- \*\*'` and by confirming the same line does not match `[resolved` or an em-dash.

The new bullet back-references the adjacent precedent bullets by line pointer in the established house style, naming at least patterns.md:776 (the test-quality clause list it extends) and at least one of patterns.md:566, :570, :572 (the CAM-236 sweep-completeness cluster it generalizes) or patterns.md:772, :774 (the CAM-301/CAM-309 self-nullifying-oracle antipattern it neighbours).
Quality gates green: `bun run typecheck` zero errors, `bun test` zero failures with the count at or above main's baseline, `bun run check:all` passing.
gotchas: patterns.md has NO sections. It is one `# Codebase Patterns` heading, a 6-line preamble, then a flat blank-line-separated list of top-level `- ` bullets to EOF (897 lines). The agent docs in scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md and .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md repeatedly instruct agents to 'grep for the section', but no sections exist. The issue's own acceptance text ('placed in a section a planner would grep') rests on that false premise. Discovery is purely keyword grep over a flat list, so the bullet must be KEYWORD-DENSE: it should contain falsifiable, oracle, acceptance criterion, grep, test assertion, sweep, and main, because those are the words a future planner or implementer would actually grep for.

Many bullets inside patterns.md cross-reference other bullets BY LINE NUMBER (patterns.md:770, :776, :20, :150, :324, :454 and others, concentrated in the line-776 test-quality bullet). Inserting anywhere except EOF silently invalidates every one of those pointers. Append at EOF and nowhere else. This is also why the line-776 bullet must not be edited in place.

Do NOT amend the existing line-776 test-quality bullet. It carries a pre-existing off-by-one (it says 'Four clauses' then enumerates five). Fixing that is out of scope, and editing that line at all shifts every subsequent line number and breaks AC3. Back-reference it instead.

There is NO file-size budget entry for patterns.md and there cannot be one: the gate's glob at scripts/check-file-sizes.ts:96 is `{src,scripts,test}/**/*.{ts,tsx}` and has no .md handling. The budget file is scripts/file-size-budget.json (repo root scripts/, NOT scripts/cam/). Appending ~10 lines of markdown trips no size gate, so no budget raise and no tracker-ref ceremony applies.

Never prefix a living rule with `[resolved YYYY-MM]`. That marker means 'already-resolved one-time mechanic' and `cam patterns archive` sweeps any bullet carrying it into patterns.archive.md. patterns.md currently has zero such markers.

The falsifiability rule is genuinely new language: `grep falsifiab` over patterns.md returns zero on main. The nearest existing bullets are about oracle CORRECTNESS, not oracle FALSIFIABILITY: patterns.md:772/:774 (the `-q` plus `-L`/`-l` self-nullifying grep antipattern, CAM-301/CAM-309), :616 (structurally unsatisfiable file-count oracles), :412/:842/:588 (negative-grep oracles matching comments), and the CAM-236 sweep-completeness cluster at :566/:570/:572. Generalize and cite them; do not restate them.

The rule being authored applies recursively to this PRD's own criteria. Every oracle above was swept red against unmodified main before dispatch except AC3, which is a deliberate green-on-main pinning oracle, and AC7, which is vacuous unless AC1 matches. Both exceptions are labelled inline. Do not silently add an unlabelled green-on-main criterion to this PRD.
domainTerms: oracle: the executable shell or assertion expression a criterion is checked by, as distinct from the criterion's prose intent
falsifiable oracle: an oracle proven to FAIL against unmodified main before it is pinned, so that its passing after the change carries information
red-sweep: running EVERY oracle in a PRD against unmodified main and confirming each fails, as opposed to spot-checking a sample, which is precisely what let CAM-368's AC6c through
pinning oracle: a deliberately green-on-main regression guard asserting that something does NOT change, exempt from the red-first duty because it makes no claim about new behavior
